title: Vijay Makes History as Tamil Nadu's New Chief Minister
excerpt: The superstar-turned-politician breaks 59 years of Dravidian rule — then a song-order row steals the spotlight.
body:
C. Joseph Vijay, founder of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), was sworn in as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister on Sunday morning at Chennai's Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium — closing a remarkable two-year journey from cinema icon to the state's highest office.

**What happened at the ceremony:**
Vijay took the oath at 10 AM, with Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar administering the Oath of Office and Secrecy. Nine ministers were sworn in alongside him. Congress opposition leader Rahul Gandhi attended, his presence carrying political weight well beyond ceremony. Vijay also became the first actor in Tamil Nadu's history to secure a majority mandate and assume office as Chief Minister in his very first electoral contest.

**Why this moment reshapes Indian politics:**
Vijay made history as the first Chief Minister of the state since 1967 who does not come from either the DMK or the AIADMK. He secured the backing of 120 MLAs-elect in the 234-member House, with support from Congress, CPI, CPI(M), VCK and IUML. Soon after the swearing-in, he signed three files to implement poll-time promises, including 200 units of free power to domestic consumers and a special force for women's safety.

**The song-order row that followed:**
The ceremony started with all six stanzas of 'Vande Mataram', followed by 'Jana Gana Mana' and the state song 'Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu' — in line with a Union Home Ministry directive from January 28 requiring 'Vande Mataram' to precede the national anthem at all official functions. The CPI criticised the conduct, questioning why 'Tamil Thai Vaazhthu' was relegated to third place — against the long-standing convention of giving the Tamil invocation primacy. TVK Minister Aadhav Arjuna attributed the sequence to 'a new circular from the Union government' and affirmed the practice will no longer be followed in the state.

**What to watch next:**
Vijay must prove his majority on the floor of the Assembly through a confidence motion on or before May 13 — a tight deadline that will test his slim two-seat margin and the durability of his coalition.
nri_angle: For Indian-Americans with Tamil roots, Vijay's rise signals a generational political reset in the state — one with direct implications for language rights, federalism, and the cultural identity many in the diaspora still hold dear.
author: Diaspora Desk
